podcast.title: "All a Dream" Series Finale (1997)
podcast.body: The final episode, aired on May 20, 1997, concluded with Barr delivering a voiceover revealing that the entire ninth season was a fantasy of her depressed character. The lottery win had not happened, and Dan had actually died from the heart attack he suffered at the end of season 8. Barr viewed this ending as representing her "total control" over the show, and the rest of the cast was unaware of this game-changing twist. "For Bar, this last episode represented her total control over the show."

podcast.title: Cancellation of Reboot Due to Twitter Rant (2018)
podcast.body: The 2018 reboot of Roseanne was canceled two months after Barr posted a racist Twitter rant against Valerie Jarrett, a former adviser to President Barack Obama. "The show was canceled two months later after Bar went on a racist Twitter rant against Valerie Jarrett, a former adviser to President Barack Obama."

podcast.title: Appearance on The Tonight Show with Johnny Carson
podcast.body: Barr gained attention after appearing on The Tonight Show with Johnny Carson to perform her stand-up routine. At the time, she was not nationally known, believed to be from Denver, and her appearance on the show, hosted by Johnny Carson, was considered the "holy grail" for comedians. "She was kind of not known at all, certainly not nationally. I believe she was out of Denver at the time when she went on the Tonight Show."

podcast.title: Behind-the-Scenes Conflict with Matt Williams
podcast.body: From the beginning, there was trouble behind the scenes. At the premiere screening party, Barr realized the "created by" credit went solely to writer Matt Williams, which enraged her as she felt the show was built around her actual life. This led to a "burning hatred" for Williams, constant pushback, refusal of lines, tantrums, and walking off set. The situation escalated until executive producers Carsey and Werner were forced to choose, resulting in Williams being asked to leave in the middle of the first season. "When the credits flashed up on the screen, Barr realized for the first time that the created by credit went solely to writer Matt Williams."

podcast.title: Character Killed Off in Spin-off
podcast.body: Following the cancellation of the Roseanne reboot, ABC launched a spin-off called The Conners, which continued without the matriarch. In this spin-off, the character of Roseanne Conner was killed off by an opioid overdose. "In the end, Drozan was killed off by an opioid overdose."

podcast.title: Control and Backstage Drama with Tom Arnold
podcast.body: After Matt Williams left, Barr added her new husband, Tom Arnold, to the writing team. Arnold also played a reoccurring character but was notorious for causing drama backstage. He acted as Barr's "henchman," executing her demands and routine firings. The couple exerted significant power over scripts, rewriting them after each read-through, which caused tension among the constantly changing writing staff. "He was basically served as Barr's henchman, executing her often crazy demands and routine firings."

podcast.title: Domestic Goddess Persona
podcast.body: Her persona was described as the "domestic goddess," which, according to TV critic Paul Brownfield, was authentic and working-class, fitting what the network was looking for. "Everything about her seemed very authentic. And her persona was the domestic goddess."

podcast.title: Emmy Nominations and Wins
podcast.body: Despite its sharp comedy and "segment-busting storylines," the series was never nominated for a best comedy series Emmy. However, Barr eventually won an Emmy for her performance on the series. "But both Barr and Laurie Metcalf, who played Rosanne's sister Jackie, eventually walked away with Emmys for their performance on the series."

podcast.title: Lack of Acting Cred
podcast.body: Despite her success as a comedian, she had no prior acting experience, which the production team considered a challenge and felt it was imperative to pair her with a skilled actor like John Goodman. "There was a comedian. She had no acting cred."

podcast.title: Season 5 Egg-Printed Shirt Running Joke
podcast.body: After Barr and Arnold split in May 1994, the show entered "surreal territory," exemplified by a season-long running joke where each of the Conners appeared in different scenes wearing the same long-sleeved, egg-printed shirt with a large chicken on the front, with no explanation. "You can forget season 5's running joke in which each of the Conners appears in a different scene in the same long-sleeved, egg-printed shirt with a large chicken on the front."

podcast.title: Tabloid Dominance
podcast.body: Barr and Tom Arnold's "wild relationship" frequently dominated the tabloids during the show's run. "Barr also dominated the tabloids with her wild relationship with Arnold."

xref.title: Casting as Dan Conner in Roseanne
xref.body: Barr told Entertainment Weekly in 2008 that Goodman was the only person who read for the role of Dan Conner in Roseanne, despite more readings being planned. She "fell in love with him" the moment she met him. He had previously gained attention on Broadway. "He said, there were more planned, but the second I met that guy, I fell in love with him."
